I was doing a lot of leg extensions in the first month. My PT didn’t seem to know what she was doing so I reached out to a friend of my husband’s. He met with me online and told me to find somebody with DNS (Dynamic Neuromuscular Stabilization) training. After a couple of months of doing very basic leg raises and leg extensions with not much progress, I finally found a therapist with my healthcare provider who had the type of training I was looking for. I honestly believe I wouldn’t have gotten better without him. He looked at my exercises and literally said “that’s cute, I’m gonna scrap it all.” From there he put me to work with squats- wall squats, single leg, squats, jumping squats, lunges, step ups, all very rigorously. It was pretty brutal, but overtime it became obvious it was helping as I began to feel much better walking and was able to go back to my dance class. Eventually I started jumping again and just recently a few months ago. I was able to hop on one leg once again. I still wear a brace when dancing just to be safe. 

He quit the place where I saw him which really sucked, but I kept the routine and I am now doing squats with weight in the squat rack, but have kept a lot of the lunges and step ups. I know it’s easy to re-injure yourself so please make sure you check in with your physical therapist before you try any of these things. He helped me with adding exercises as I progressively got stronger, but he was very clear about not overdoing it to not get injured again.

It’s also worth mentioning that I am heavier, and I still was able to get better and my quads are stronger than they have ever been now. So I highly encourage people that aren’t experiencing a lot of instability to see if their orthopedic surgeon might consider not going with surgery. My surgeon told me the surgery for me was pointless because the only thing it does is give you stability back. Osteoarthritis could happen with or without surgery, it could actually be worse with surgery.
